title: Config Parser
story: Your app reads configuration from a file. Each config value could be a number ("42"), a text string ("localhost"), or a yes/no flag ("true"). You need one type that holds any of these, a way to display them, and a safe way to extract numbers.
why: An enum with typed variant data is how apps handle mixed-type configuration values safely.
analogy: ConfigValue is like a universal adapter plug. Number is the numeric prong, Text is the string port, YesNo is the binary switch. The display method translates each variant into a human-readable label. as_number tries to pull a number out of any plug — it works with the numeric prong and makes a best-effort guess for the others.
try_it: Add a `ConfigValue.Range(low: Int, high: Int)` variant with two Int values. Update `display` to show "range: low-high". Update `as_number` to return the midpoint: `(low + high) / 2`. Create and test a range value.
tips: Use `_` wildcard when you don't need the variant's data: `Text(_)` means "I know it's text, I just don't need the string"
`as_number` provides a safe default (0) instead of crashing — this is the "defensive extraction" pattern
Bool can be converted to Int: `if b { return 1; }` — there's no automatic bool-to-int conversion
common_mistakes: Trying to access data without matching first: you can't write `v.n` directly
Returning a string from `as_number` for Text variants — the return type is Int, so you must return a number
